sentences: The bodhisattva sits with one leg resting across the other knee, fingertips barely touching the cheek, lost in thought.
In Korean the pose is called bangasayu: half-cross-legged, contemplating.
The upper body is pared down and smooth, while the skirt below ripples like water, giving rhythm to a still figure.
Above all, the faint smile at the corners of the mouth suggests not anguish but the calm that comes just before enlightenment.
Casting gilt bronze this thin at this size, in such balance, was the highest technical achievement of its time.
Today two pensive bodhisattvas sit side by side in the museum's dedicated Room of Quiet Contemplation.
